chunks: I have come to know that you have razed the ground and taken away whatever was under your feet and devoured whatever was in your hands,
and know that the accounting to Allah will be severer than that to the people;
and that is an end to the matter.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali's letter to his officers say about accountability and wealth?
ai.summary: In this epistle, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of 'clearing the earth' to critique the officer's monopolization of public resources, contrasting their limited administrative audit with the ultimate, comprehensive reckoning of Allah. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adl* (justice) and the moral responsibility of leaders to avoid *ghul* (extraction beyond due share), serving as a timeless warning that worldly authority is merely a trust subject to divine scrutiny.
